title: Prayer
note: Rebuilt on 2026-11-26 from the Bible Explorer film of the same slug. New wording, same facts: each claim is in the old film's captions or its 'differ' note, whose sources are in docs/work/elite/explorer-ledger.md. Scripture is the Berean Standard Bible, checked against client/public/bible/text/ by film/tools/write-script.py.

lines: Prayer is talking with God, who is our Father: bringing him worship, thanks, confession, and requests, and trusting that he hears because of Jesus.
It's not a way of getting things out of God. It's a child speaking to a father.

When his disciples asked him to teach them to pray, Jesus gave them a pattern, the Lord's Prayer. God's name honored. His kingdom and his will first. Then daily bread, forgiveness as we forgive, and protection from evil.
Your kingdom come, Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
Christians all over the world still pray it.

scripture.text: Your kingdom come, Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.

lines: Praise tells God who he is. Thanks tells him what he has done.
The psalms, the Bible's own book of prayers and songs, are full of both.

scripture.text: Enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise

lines: Paul tells worried people not to swallow their worry but to turn it into prayer, with thanks.
Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.
Asking is not bothering God. It's what children do with a father who loves them.

scripture.text: Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.

lines: Confession is neither groveling nor hiding. When we sin we confess it to God, who is faithful and just to forgive us because of Jesus, and we turn from it.
There is no sin too big for the cross.

scripture.text: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins

chapters.kicker: When the answer is not what we asked
lines: Prayer is not a promise that we will get what we ask. Jesus himself asked his Father in the garden to take the cup of suffering away, and added these words.
Yet not My will, but Yours be done.
Some prayers, even for someone to get better, are not answered the way we longed for, and that hurts. The Bible doesn't hide it. Many of its prayers ask God: how long, O LORD?

scripture.text: Yet not My will, but Yours be done.

lines: Paul says that when we don't know how we ought to pray, the Spirit himself prays for us, with groans too deep for words.
Prayer doesn't depend on finding the right words. It rests on God, who wants to hear.

scripture.text: the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groans too deep for words.

lines: It's a child speaking to a father.
titleCard: A child speaking to a father.
